title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 233 (Merger or amalgamation of certain companies)

content.overview: Section 233 provides a fast-track merger or amalgamation route for eligible classes of companies (including small companies, a holding company and its wholly owned subsidiary, and start-ups as notified; later rules may widen eligibility — the class in force on the filing date must be checked). The scheme is approved by members holding at least ninety per cent of the total share capital and by creditors representing nine-tenths in value, then filed with the Central Government (Regional Director). Objections by the Registrar or official liquidator can result in the scheme being referred to the Tribunal under the ordinary process. Confirmation is by the Central Government through the Regional Director, without the ordinary full Tribunal process unless so referred.
content.glance: Fast-track for eligible classes (small cos, holding–WOS, start-ups as notified; check current rules): 90% members + 9/10 creditors; RD confirmation; ROC/OL objection may remit to Tribunal.
content.study: A scheme of merger or amalgamation may be entered into between two or more small companies, or between a holding company and its wholly owned subsidiary company, or such other class or classes of companies as may be prescribed, and approved by members holding at least ninety per cent of the total number of shares and by creditors representing nine-tenths in value, then filed with the Central Government. The Registrar and official liquidator may make objections; if objections are sustained, the Central Government may refer the scheme to the Tribunal. Current-law framing: confirm eligibility class in force on the filing date; obtain 90% member and 9/10 creditor approvals; file with RD; address ROC/OL objections; obtain CG confirmation through RD, or face remittal to Tribunal under the ordinary route.

sections.heading: Eligibility
sections.body: Small companies; holding company and its wholly owned subsidiary; start-ups as notified; other prescribed classes — check rules in force on filing date.

sections.heading: Approvals
sections.body: Members holding at least ninety per cent of total share capital; creditors representing nine-tenths in value.

sections.heading: Process
sections.body: File scheme with Central Government (Regional Director); ROC and official liquidator may object; sustained objection may refer scheme to Tribunal.

sections.heading: Confirmation
sections.body: Confirmed by Central Government through Regional Director without ordinary full Tribunal process, unless referred.

provisions.title: Merger or amalgamation of certain companies

examples.title: Holding–WOS fast-track
examples.body: A holding company merges its wholly owned subsidiary under s. 233. With 90% member and 9/10 creditor approvals and no sustained ROC/OL objection, the Regional Director may confirm the scheme without a full Tribunal process.

examples.title: Objection remits to Tribunal
examples.body: The official liquidator objects to a fast-track scheme on solvency grounds. If the Central Government refers the scheme to the Tribunal, the ordinary s. 232 process applies.

hypotheticals.question: Can any two listed companies use s. 233 to avoid the Tribunal?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 233 is limited to prescribed eligible classes (small companies, holding–WOS, start-ups as notified, and other classes prescribed by rules). Ordinary mergers of companies outside those classes use s. 232.

distinctions.title: Fast-track merger (s. 233) vs Tribunal merger (s. 232)
distinctions.left: Eligible classes; 90% members / 9/10 creditors; RD confirmation
distinctions.right: Full Tribunal process; valuation and RD/OL reports for all mergers

misconceptions.trap: Any company can choose the fast-track route to avoid Tribunal scrutiny.
misconceptions.correction: Section 233 is available only to prescribed eligible classes. Companies outside those classes must use the ordinary Tribunal route under s. 232.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 233 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm eligibility class. II. Check 90% members and 9/10 creditors. III. File with RD; address objections. IV. Confirmation or remittal to Tribunal. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Eligibility; approvals; objections; confirmation sought; precise relief.

enhancement.definition: Section 233 provides a fast-track merger or amalgamation for prescribed eligible companies, approved by 90% of members and nine-tenths of creditors by value, and confirmed by the Central Government through the Regional Director, subject to ROC/OL objection and possible remittal to the Tribunal.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Low-complexity intra-group and small-company mergers can proceed through a streamlined Central Government confirmation route while preserving an objection path to the Tribunal.
essentialIngredients: Eligible class under the Act and rules in force
Approval by members holding at least 90% of share capital
Approval by creditors representing 9/10 in value
File with CG (RD); confirmation unless referred to Tribunal on objection
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 233 is the fast-track alternative to the ordinary s. 232 Tribunal merger.
enhancement.problemApplication: Confirm class; check thresholds; file; address objections.
